confirmed.title: After a conflict, every later save of that case/reflection on the device says saved but is never sent, stays hidden, and is thrown away when the conflict is resolved
confirmed.scenario: 1) The phone, offline, edits case X (base v1). The laptop edits X online (v2). 2) The phone reconnects. Its edit conflicts and the header says 'Save needs attention'. X now shows the laptop's version, because overlay() shows conflict.remote (writes.js:96-97). 3) Still on the phone, the resident edits X again, for example re-typing the change or adding a tag (updateCase -> writes.save). The new job is queued behind the conflict. drain() always takes the oldest unfinished job for the record, which is the conflict, and stops at `job.state !== 'pending'` (writes.js:19-20). The job never runs, and 'Retry sync' on it does nothing. Yet save() resolves after the 180 ms race and marks the job accepted (writes.js:85-88), so the dialog closes as saved. The list still shows conflict.remote, so the edit appears to revert. In the reflection editor, every autosave after a conflict shows 'Saved locally · pending sync'. 4) The resident opens Recent changes and taps 'Keep version from elsewhere' (ui-recovery.js:54) or 'Restore my version' (ui-recovery.js:16). Both call writes.archive(job.key), which archives every unfinished job of that record (writes.js:108), including the later edits. 5) Variant: the resident deletes X after the conflict. moveToBin writes the bin entry first; its data is the shown version, i.e. the remote. The delete job is then stuck behind the conflict. Every other device's bin feed drops X (its stamp is not newer than the tombstone) while X is still on the server. Resolving with 'Keep version from elsewhere' archives the delete, and X stays hidden on those devices until their weekly full read.
confirmed.consequence: Data loss and false 'saved'. Case edits and reflection text written after a conflict never reach the server. Either resolution button silently discards them; they survive only as an 'archived' history entry on that one device, which is cleared at sign-out and pruned after 100. A delete made after a conflict hides a live case on every other device, so their counts and Totals drop. This is also a likely root cause of the parked Firefox seed 285932884 'stale copy': the overlay pins job.remote from the time of the conflict. Daily notes have their own merge (ui-notepad.js healClosed); cases and reflections have nothing.
confirmed.fix: In writes.save, when the record has an unresolved conflict job, treat the new save as resolving it. Archive only the conflict job (it stays in history) and use conflict.remote as the new job's base, since the user edited what was shown. Alternatively, reject the save with a clear 'resolve it in Recent changes first' error so the editor keeps the text. In overlay(), let a later accepted job win over a conflict, and otherwise show the live list rather than a frozen remote. In archive(), archive only the chosen job and older ones, never later saves.
verifier_fix:
The direction is right, but one part of the proposed fix is unsafe. It would always use conflict.remote as the new job's base. The reflection editor's session.base is the device's own earlier save, not the remote. A case dialog opened before the conflict arrived also has base = the phone's own version. Forcing base = remote for those saves would silently overwrite the other device's change.

Better:

1. **In save(), when the record has a conflict job:**
   - If recordSignature(base) === recordSignature(conflict.remote), the user edited the version that was shown. Archive only that conflict job (it stays in history) and queue the new job with the caller's base. The backend transaction still checks that base against the server, so a further change elsewhere still conflicts.
   - Otherwise, do not mark the new job accepted. Either store it straight away as state 'conflict' with remote = conflict.remote, superseding the old conflict job, or throw a clear 'This record changed elsewhere; resolve it in Recent changes' error so the editor keeps its text. Never return an accepted pending job that cannot run.
2. **'Restore my version'** (ui-recovery.js restore) should save the newest pending/conflict record of the chain, as healClosed does with group[0], not the oldest conflict job's record.
3. **overlay():** a job that superseded a conflict wins naturally. While a conflict still stands, the UI should not report later saves as saved.
4. **Delete after a conflict:** with fix 1, the delete runs (its base is the remote) or is marked conflict, so watchDeletes rolls back the bin entry. Also make watchDeletes treat 'archived' after a never-synced delete as a failure, so the bin entry comes back out.
5. **Tests:** add a writes.test.mjs case: conflict, then save with base = remote, which must reach the server; and save with base = own version, which must not be accepted.

confirmed.title: Moving a reflection to the recycle bin deletes it without checking for newer edits, so an edit saved on another device is lost and the bin keeps the older version
confirmed.scenario: 1) Reflection R is on the phone and the laptop (v1). 2) The phone, offline in theatre or simply holding a stale list, moves R to the recycle bin. moveToBin saves the bin entry (data = the phone's v1) and calls cloud.deleteReflection, which runs an unconditional F.deleteDoc (cloud.js:540-544) and queues it in Firestore's offline queue. 3) Meanwhile, on the laptop, the resident writes the long version of R. The editor's write queue commits v2 to the server. 4) The phone gets signal. Firestore sends the bin entry and the delete. The delete removes v2: no base check, and no rules check. The laptop's listener drops R. The recycle bin offers only the phone's v1.
confirmed.consequence: The laptop's reflection text disappears from the logbook. Its only remaining copy is the laptop's device-only Recent changes history, which is gone if the resident signed out (for example on a ward PC). This is the race #523 fixed for cases: they now go through the write queue with the version being deleted as base, and a refused delete is undone with a toast. Notes do the same. Reflections were left on the blind delete. The reflection metadata writes are also blind full-document setDocs from the device's possibly stale copy (setExport, justEnough and its Undo, completeSelected, moveReflection and its Undo in ui-reflect.js). They overwrite a concurrent text edit the same way, with no bin copy at all.
confirmed.fix: In moveToBin's reflection branch, delete through `writes.save('reflection', owner, { id: e.data.id, _deleted: true }, item)` and call watchDeletes(owner, kind, ok), as the note branch does; commitRecord already supports reflections. rollBack already handles the conflict toast for queued deletes. Route the metadata saves through writes.save with the shown version as base.
verifier_fix:
In moveToBin's reflection branch, delete through the write queue as notes do:
- `writes.save('reflection', owner, { id: e.data.id, _deleted: true }, base)`, then `watchDeletes(owner, kind, ok)`.
- The base must be the last saved version, not the editor's working copy: `(S.reflections || []).find(x => x.id === e.data.id) || item`. Alternatively, have the editor's Delete call `await persist()` first (or pass `session.base`) while the bin entry keeps the working copy.

In rollBack, remove the `kind !== 'reflection' &&` guard. A failed or conflicting reflection delete job is then archived, and a conflict shows the "changed on another device, so it was kept" toast and `continue`s, instead of falling through to `cloud.saveReflection(owner, { ...e.data })`, which blindly writes the old v1 over the newer version.

Change rollBack's non-conflict restore for reflections to `writes.save('reflection', owner, { ...e.data }, e.data)` rather than the blind `cloud.saveReflection`.

Add a reflection case to conflicts.emulator.mjs: an offline delete on one device against an online edit on the other.

Separately, route the reflection metadata saves in ui-reflect.js through `writes.save` with the shown version as base: setExport, the export picker and its Undo, completeSelected, moveReflection and its Undo, and the bulk export toggle.

confirmed.title: The recycle bin hides a case on every device before its delete is safely queued, and the restore or re-save meant to undo that writes nothing
confirmed.scenario: A) The resident deletes case X with no signal. saveBinEntry's write enters Firestore's offline queue at once. The tomb feed applies the local snapshot immediately (sync.js:232), so X leaves the list and the device's store records it as gone. moveToBin then waits ACK_WAIT (3 s, cloud.js:110) before removeCase, the step that records the delete in the write queue. If the app is swiped away or killed in those 3 s, no delete exists anywhere. Next time online, Firestore sends the bin entry; every device drops X, but the server keeps it. Each device's weekly full read (replaceAll ignores `gone`) brings X back. The bin feed's own weekly full read can drop it again until the entry is purged at 30 days. After that, X is back for good. B) The resident taps Restore or Undo on that entry. restoreFromBin -> restoreCase(out, null) -> commitRecord. The server copy equals the bin copy except for updatedAt, and checkWrite ignores updatedAt (recovery-store.js:82), so nothing is written (cloud.js:456/467). The bin entry is then deleted. No listener event reaches any engine, so X stays hidden everywhere and is no longer in the bin. rollBack's 'saved again, stamped after that version' (bin.js:112) is the same no-op. So a delete that fails with a non-transient error, or a recovery-store failure in writes.save, leaves the case invisible on all devices and out of the bin. Finding 1's stuck delete feeds into this too.
confirmed.consequence: A case that exists on the server is hidden on every device and absent from the bin. Totals and summaries undercount. The app says 'Case restored' but no case appears. Up to a week later, at each device's full read, the deleted case comes back on its own: the same symptom as #519, by a different route.
confirmed.fix: (1) In moveToBin, persist the delete job (writes.save) before awaiting the bin write's ack. It can still drain only after the bin entry is acknowledged, but the intent then survives a kill. (2) Let restores and rollBack force a write when only updatedAt differs, for example a `touch` flag that skips the equality short-circuit in commitRecord, or an updateDoc({updatedAt: now}) after a no-op restore. Devices that applied the tombstone then receive the record again. (3) Optionally, when a tombstone arrives only from the cache, confirm the record is gone (fetchOne) before dropping it.
verifier_fix:
Fix (2) needs care. If a `touch` flag simply skips the equality check, restoreFromBin (base = null, server still has X) falls through to the conflict check and throws write-conflict. Instead, when the content is equal and touch is set, commitRecord should write the stamp (tx.set(doc), or update updatedAt) rather than return false, without going on to the base comparison. Use the flag for both restoreFromBin and rollBack. The "updateDoc({updatedAt: now}) after a no-op" variant also works.

For part A, fix (1) as stated could let the delete reach the server before a bin write that the rules then refuse, so the write queue would need a 'held until the bin entry is acknowledged' state. A simpler option: in purgeExpired, which already reads the whole bin once a day, call fetchOne for each case entry. If the original is still on the server at or before the binned version and no delete job exists, either finish the move (removeCase with base = e.data) or re-stamp the case and drop the entry.

Strengthen bugfixes.mjs to check that the re-save actually changed the server's updatedAt, or that a second device shows the case.

confirmed.title: A deleted case comes back under its other id: the Form inbox and the workbook import only recognise deletions made under their own id
confirmed.scenario: (a) A Form response reached the logbook through the Admin workbook import (imp_ id), as the 1-14 Oct responses and the 14 Oct re-import did. The resident deletes that case into the bin, for example one of a duplicate pair. The Form script then sends the response again. This happens with logbookInboxBackfill, whose comment (Code.gs:159) says it leaves out 'ones the resident deleted. Safe to run again'. It also happens when the resident edits the response, since 'Allow response editing' stays ON. pickUpForm passes the bin's case ids (app.js:1087), but mergeFormEntries checks only formCaseId(response) (form-inbox.js:86), and the duplicate check (line 87) looks only at live cases. A new Form case is saved, and the deleted case is back. (b) The reverse: a response that came in through the inbox (form id) is deleted by the resident. Later the owner imports the workbook, whose rows for that response are not in imports/{rid}. withoutFormCases(rows, listCases) (ui-admin.js:414) knows only live Form cases, so the row is imported as imp_ and the case is back. The fix on branch fix/import-no-overwrite (c077455) passes only live ids as `have`, so it doesn't cover this.
confirmed.consequence: Cases the resident deliberately deleted reappear as new cases. This includes duplicates like one resident's two from 11 Oct, which the owner also removed from the sheet; the Form still holds those responses, so a backfill would bring them back. The app's counts, Totals and the drift check against the response sheet then differ.
confirmed.fix: (a) In pickUpForm, pass the bin's case entries' data, not just their ids. In mergeFormEntries, treat a response as gone when a binned case is the same response (run isImportOf against the binned data as well as live cases). (b) Admins can't read the bin, so record the identity of deleted responses where the import can see it: when a resident bins a 'form' or 'import' case, add its response key or submittedAt to the logbook doc, which the app owner can read. withoutFormCases then skips those rows. Also correct the backfill's 'Safe to run again' comment until then.
verifier_fix:
The proposal is mostly right. Three refinements:

1. Part (a) does not cover edited responses. An edit changes submittedAt, so sameResponse() fails for a binned imp_ case, and also for a live one (that already makes a duplicate today). Matching on bin data only covers re-sends with the same timestamp, such as the backfill. Say so in the README and Code.gs. Also change the backfill's default SINCE to the last import date (not 1 Oct), or make SINCE required.
   - In pickUpForm, pass the bin's case data: `bin.filter(b => b.kind === 'case' && b.data).map(b => b.data)`.
   - In mergeFormEntries, treat a response as gone when `inBin.has(cid)` or any binned case satisfies `isImportOf(b, e, r.case)`.
   - Add a test with a binned imp_ case.

2. For (b), validLogbook uses keys().hasOnly, so adding a deleted-responses field to the logbook doc needs a rules change and rules tests. A cheaper option needs no rules change: when the resident's device sees a new case with source 'import' that matches a binned 'form' case (sameDay and sameResponse on createdAt), it removes the new case. Another option: the Admin import shows rows that have no live match and are newer than the inbox go-live date (14 Oct), and asks the owner to confirm them.

3. Correct the drift-check skill's "rows already in the app or its bin are skipped" until (b) is fixed.
